items.t: Grandview-Woodland runs from Clark Drive (west) to Kamloops Street (east), East 12th Avenue / Grandview Highway (south) to Burrard Inlet (north) — the boundaries of the Grandview-Woodland Community Plan study area. Nearby areas: Hastings-Sunrise north-east, Mount Pleasant west, Renfrew-Collingwood south-east, Strathcona north-west.

Where the condo stock concentrates: on the two commercial spines — Commercial Drive (Marquee on the Drive, Life on the Drive, ACE at East 12th) and East Hastings Street (Bohème at the north end of the Drive), with East Broadway product at the south edge (Popolo).
Main streets: Commercial Drive and East Hastings Street are the commercial spines; Clark Drive, Nanaimo Street, Victoria Drive, East Broadway and East 12th Avenue / Grandview Highway frame the area.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus stops at Hastings and Commercial; TransLink route 20 runs on Commercial Drive and Victoria Drive; Commercial-Broadway Station (Expo and Millennium Lines) sits at the area's south-west edge.

A cinema became a condo without leaving. Marquee on the Drive reused more than 75 percent of the Van East Cinema's structure — the heritage-feeling façade on Commercial Drive is the old theatre, not a replica.

Bohème is two tenures in one envelope. The complex at 1588 East Hastings holds 82 strata condos plus a separate 20-unit rental air-space parcel — "Bohème" listings and "Bohème" rentals are different legal products at the same address.

The area plan is a named plan, not a vibe. The Grandview-Woodland Community Plan (with the citywide Vancouver Plan over it) is the document that sets the low-scale, early-1900s character the area markets on — and the reason corridor density concentrates on Commercial, Hastings and Broadway instead of the interior streets.

χpey̓ Elementary carries an Indigenous name in the district directory. The school at 1950 East Hastings Street is listed by the VSB under its Musqueam name — a detail that trips up address searches run under older school names.
Popolo's completion year is genuinely unsettled in public sources.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Grandview-Woodland

items.t: Municipality: City of Vancouver, BC.

Boundaries (Grandview-Woodland Community Plan study area, as stated in the City profile): Clark Drive to the west, Kamloops Street to the east, East 12th Avenue and Grandview Highway segments to the south, and Burrard Inlet to the north. A parcel at the edge should be checked against the City's local-area map.
Nearby areas: Strathcona to the west (across Clark Drive), Hastings-Sunrise to the east, Kensington-Cedar Cottage to the south, and Renfrew-Collingwood to the south-east.

Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage in Jared's FVR + GVR September 2026 reports — there is no Vancouver section, and no substitute stats source is used. Sub-area inventory, solds and medians: Not verified.

Schools: SD39 (Vancouver School Board) catchments are address-based; SD39 has no middle-school tier — elementary is Kindergarten to Grade 7 and secondary is Grades 8 to 12. Schools located in the area: Lord Nelson Elementary, 1355 Garden Drive; χpey̓ Elementary, 1950 East Hastings Street; Britannia Elementary, 1110 Cotton Drive; and Britannia Secondary, 1001 Cotton Drive.

Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs from Burrard Station to SFU Exchange with stops at Hastings at Commercial, Nanaimo and Renfrew; routes 14, 16 and 20 also serve Hastings Street, and route 20 runs on Commercial Drive and Victoria Drive. Commercial-Broadway Station, at the area's south-west edge, provides Expo Line and Millennium Line service.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Grandview-Woodland

items.t: City zoning frame: house lots sit under the R1-1 District Schedule of Zoning and Development By-law No. 3575 — minimum site area 306 m² for a multiple dwelling with 3 or 4 units, a duplex or a single detached house, 464 m² for 5 units, and 557 m² for 6, 7 or 8 units; single detached houses may include a secondary suite and a laneway house, and duplexes may include secondary suites and lock-off units; a multiplex of up to 6 units, or up to 8 rental units, is possible on qualifying lots. RT districts also apply on parts of the area's older house stock; the zone and district for a specific lot: Not verified.

Form B diligence (strata product, including the Woodland Block presale's strata form and the apartment strata): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page.
Fee-simple townhomes / house forms: A multiplex lot's unit potential is a zoning-schedule question (R1-1 figures above), not a strata question.

The hyphen is the tell. The City's official name is "Grandview-Woodland"; the board's common form drops the hyphen. Copy that cannot settle the name usually cannot settle the boundary either — and the boundary is what decides whether edge projects like The Cut are in this market at all.
Trout Lake is at the area's southern edge, per the City — close enough to anchor southern-block marketing, far enough that "steps to Trout Lake" claims for northern blocks deserve a map check.

The area's ground was logged, then served by the Vancouver–New Westminster interurban railway, and the first houses and city water arrived along Commercial Drive — the character-house stock on the interior streets descends from that settlement pattern, which is why the RT districts still sit over parts of the older house stock.

There is no hospital inside Grandview-Woodland: the health-authority pages name Vancouver General Hospital, 899 West 12th Avenue, and Mount Saint Joseph Hospital, 3080 Prince Edward Street, for Vancouver — a hospital located inside the area itself: Not verified.

The City profile names Commercial Drive and Hastings Street as the area's main commercial shopping streets — but a specific grocery store name and civic address inside the area confirmed on an official source: Not verified. Treat any "grocery-anchored" claim for a specific block as unproven until the store is named and checked.

Flood diligence here is a dataset check, not a neighbourhood trait: the City's designated floodplain mapping is a citywide dataset covering coastal and Still Creek floodplains, and a parcel-level floodplain result for this area: Not verified — run the specific parcel rather than assuming the inlet-side blocks are or are not designated.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Grandview-Woodland

items.t: Grandview-Woodland, with a hyphen, is the City of Vancouver's official local area name, one of its 22 distinct areas — the east-side area built around Commercial Drive and East Hastings Street, between the downtown peninsula and the city's eastern neighbourhoods.

Boundaries, as stated for the Grandview-Woodland Community Plan study area: Clark Drive to the west, Kamloops Street to the east, East 12th Avenue and Grandview Highway segments to the south, and Burrard Inlet to the north. Those are the community plan study-area edges as published in the City profile; a parcel at the edge should be checked against the City's local-area map.

Main roads: Commercial Drive, East Hastings Street, Clark Drive, Nanaimo Street, Victoria Drive and East Broadway are the main streets named in City sources for this area. Transit: the R5 Hastings St RapidBus runs from Burrard Station to SFU Exchange with stops at Hastings at Commercial, Nanaimo and Renfrew, and routes 14, 16 and 20 also serve Hastings Street; route 20 runs on Commercial Drive and Victoria Drive between Downtown and the Victoria Drive / Harrison Drive area; Commercial-Broadway Station, at the area's south-west edge, provides Expo Line and Millennium Line service. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Civic core: the Britannia Community Services Centre site — with the Britannia Branch of Vancouver Public Library, an elementary school, a skating rink, a fitness facility and a swimming pool — is the area's recreation core, and the City is working with partners on the Britannia Renewal to renew and revitalize the site and the larger Britannia lands. Trout Lake sits at the area's southern edge. A hospital located inside Grandview-Woodland itself: Not verified.

Shopping: the City profile names Commercial Drive and Hastings Street as the area's main commercial shopping streets. A specific grocery store name and civic address inside the area confirmed on an official source: Not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Grandview-Woodland

items.t: Community plan / SSMUH position as the City states it: the Grandview-Woodland Community Plan is the area-specific plan over the base zoning, and the Vancouver Plan is the citywide plan that sits over it.

Floodplain / hazard diligence: the City's designated floodplain mapping is a citywide dataset covering coastal and Still Creek floodplains, and a parcel-level floodplain check for this area: Not verified — run the parcel check rather than assuming an interior-street lot is clear. No ALR land is identified in City sources for this area; ALR status remains a parcel-level check.

Older-strata diligence on the arterials: for older strata on the arterials, review the strata documents under the provincial strata framework early; BC strata disputes can go to the Civil Resolution Tribunal. Where a strata lot is involved, the full BC strata block applies (Form B diligence; depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2 with the May 1, 2023 exemptions; a "45+" listing line is not a valid BC age bylaw).

ALR rules (for completeness — no Grandview-Woodland ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an error. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

The hyphen is the tell: the City's official name is "Grandview-Woodland"; the board's common form drops the hyphen. Copy that cannot settle the name usually cannot settle the boundary either — and the boundary is what decides whether edge projects like The Cut are in this market at all.

One civic site carries the area's school, library, rink, pool and fitness core at once: the Britannia Community Services Centre site bundles the library branch, an elementary school, a skating rink, a fitness facility and a swimming pool, and its renewal (Britannia Renewal) covers the larger Britannia lands — interior lots within a short walk price that bundle, not a single amenity.
